caption:
Elon Musk says that next year he will give one of his own SpaceX shares to every kid in America.
At Friday's closing price, that is a gift worth a little over $10.5 billion.
He made the pledge a day after Anthropic announced its Public Benefit Fund, and calls it "the first of many."

Would you hold on to your kid's SpaceX share or sell it?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Axios · Photo: AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson

slides.headline: Elon Musk just promised a SpaceX share to *every kid in America*

slides.heading: One post, *72 million* kids
paras: On Monday, Musk wrote on X: "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many."
There are just over 72 million people under 18 in the U.S., according to Census Bureau figures cited by Axios.

image.credit: Fabrice Coffrini / AFP via Getty Images

slides.heading: A *$10.5 billion* gift
paras: SpaceX shares closed at $146.03 on Friday. At that price, one share per child adds up to a little over $10.5 billion.
Musk owns billions of SpaceX shares, so Axios notes the giveaway would barely dent his stake.

slides.heading: Sparked by *Anthropic*
paras: On Sunday, Anthropic said it will commit 5% of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund, pending stockholder approval.
Musk replied: "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public." Then he added: "This is what I will be doing." A day later came the SpaceX pledge.

slides.heading: The *fine print* is missing
paras: Musk did not explain how the giveaway would work, or whether "kid" means every minor or only U.S. citizens.

paras.t: In July, SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell pledged one share to each of about 2 million children's Trump Accounts.

slides.hook: Musk promised shares to 72 million kids. Follow to find out if they actually arrive.
